description: Approximate source-commit to target-write latency of a CDC pipeline on Confluent Cloud, built only from Metrics API series and the ccloud_cdc:* recording rules.

panels.title: Approx pipeline latency (metrics-only)
panels.description: Source CDC lag + Kafka queue time from fetch lag (records_lag_max ÷ sink consume rate) + sink put-batch time, each taken as the worst value across the selected connectors. Green < 1 s, amber < 5 s, red >= 5 s. Shows '∞ stalled' when a sink is behind and consuming nothing. The committed-offset queue time is shown separately for reference. It is an estimate built from per-minute aggregates; see the notes below.

panels.title: Source CDC lag (max)
panels.description: Worst CDC source lag across the selected source connectors. -1 (no events yet) is treated as 0. Latches its last value when the source is idle.

panels.title: Kafka queue time (fetch lag)
panels.description: records_lag_max ÷ sink consume rate; worst partition of each selected sink. 0 when the sink is not behind. Shows '∞ stalled' when a sink is behind and consuming nothing.

panels.title: Sink put-batch (worst task avg)
panels.description: Worst per-task average time the selected sink connectors spend writing one batch to the target system.

panels.title: Queue time from committed offsets
panels.description: Committed consumer lag divided by consume rate on the worst backlogged topic of the selected sinks. Committed offsets include the sink's offset-commit interval, so this usually reads well above the fetch-based queue time; it is a reference, not a guaranteed bound (the consume rate counts every consumer group and is 10-minute smoothed). Shows '∞ stalled' when a backlogged topic has zero consumption. No colour thresholds.

panels.title: Latency terms over time (stacked)
panels.description: The three terms of the headline estimate stacked (queue time from fetch lag), so the tallest band shows which stage dominates. The dashed line is the queue time from committed offsets for reference; it is not part of the stack. Queue values are capped at 1 hour for display; a value at the cap means the sink is stalled or at least an hour behind.

panels.title: How to read the estimate
panels.description: Caveats of the metrics-only latency estimate.

options.content:
- **What it covers:** source commit → target write = source CDC lag + Kafka queue time from fetch lag (`records_lag_max` ÷ sink consume rate) + sink put-batch time.
- **Committed-offset queue time:** includes the sink's offset-commit interval, so it usually reads well above the fetch-based value. When the two diverge, the fetch-based value is the closer estimate.
- **Approximate:** it follows typical (median) latency, not the slowest records; with several sink tasks, fetch lag can stay small in a burst while some records take several times longer. Pauses of a few seconds (for example a task restart) may not show in per-minute metrics.
- **Worst partition, connector-wide:** `records_lag_max` is the sink's worst partition across the whole connector, so with several backlogged partitions or topics the fetch-based value can understate. Check the per-table view and the committed-offset queue time.
- **Idle sources and clock skew:** source lag compares the event's source timestamp with the connector's clock, so clock differences shift it; it keeps its last value when no events flow, and a fully stalled capture job produces no events, so it shows as idle (watch source throughput) rather than rising lag.
- **No backlog:** fetch lag is 0 and the estimate is source lag + put-batch time only; the sink's own poll-and-write cycle has no metric, so at steady state it can read somewhat below the actual latency.
- **Aggregates:** it composes worst task and partition values from per-minute aggregates; it is not the journey of a single record.

panels.title: Committed vs fetch lag
panels.description: Shows 'committed lag ≫ fetch lag (offset-commit interval)' when the committed-offset queue time is above 5 s while the sink's records_lag_max is below 100 records, i.e. the sink is reading Kafka promptly but committed offsets lag behind. Otherwise 'consistent'. If records_lag_max is not reported, the check defaults to 'consistent'. An idle sink whose committed lag stays above 0 can also trigger it.

targets.expr: ((max(ccloud_cdc:sink_queue_seconds:max{connector_id=~"$sink"}) or vector(0)) > bool 5) * ((max(confluent_kafka_connect_records_lag_max{connector_id=~"$sink"}) or vector(1000000000)) < bool 100)

panels.title: records_lag_max vs committed consumer lag
panels.description: records_lag_max is the sink's fetch lag on its worst partition; committed lag is the worst topic's lag measured from the offsets the sink has committed (per topic, so it can be larger than one partition's fetch lag even without divergence). If committed lag is high while records_lag_max stays near 0, the sink is reading promptly and the difference is mostly offset-commit cadence, not a real backlog. If both rise together, the backlog is real.

panels.title: Per-table breakdown
panels.description: One row per user topic (internal topics excluded), sorted by consumer lag. Produced and Consumed are 10-minute smoothed rates; Consumed counts every consumer group of the topic. Queue time (committed) = committed lag ÷ consumed rate; it is measured to the committed offset, so it usually over-reads (shown only with backlog; 'stalled' when consumption is zero). Est. drain = lag ÷ (consumed − produced) when consumption exceeds production, otherwise '∞' while a backlog exists; '—' means no backlog.

targets.expr: (sum by (topic) (ccloud_cdc:sink_topic_lag_offsets{kafka_id="$kafka_id", connector_id=~"$sink"} > 0) / on (topic) ((sum by (topic) (ccloud_cdc:topic_consumed_records:rate10m{kafka_id="$kafka_id"}) - on (topic) (sum by (topic) (ccloud_cdc:topic_produced_records:rate10m{kafka_id="$kafka_id"}) or (0 * sum by (topic) (ccloud_cdc:topic_consumed_records:rate10m{kafka_id="$kafka_id"})))) > 0)) or (sum by (topic) (ccloud_cdc:sink_topic_lag_offsets{kafka_id="$kafka_id", connector_id=~"$sink"} > 0) * 0 + 1e12)

panels.title: Consumer lag by topic
panels.description: Committed consumer lag (offsets) of the selected sink connectors per topic. A line that keeps rising means the sink is not keeping up with production on that topic.

panels.title: Queue time by topic (committed offsets)
panels.description: Per-topic Kafka queue time from committed offsets (committed lag ÷ consumed rate), only while the topic has a backlog. It includes the sink's offset-commit interval, so it usually reads above the time records actually wait in Kafka. Values are capped at 1 hour for display; a line at the cap means the topic is stalled or at least an hour behind.

panels.title: CDC source lag (ms)
panels.description: Delay between a change being committed in the source database and the connector processing it, worst task per connector. -1 (no events yet) is shown as 0. The value latches its last reading when no events flow, and a fully stalled capture job shows as idle, not as rising lag.

panels.title: Source throughput (records/s out)
panels.description: Records per second the source connectors write to Kafka, smoothed over 10 minutes from per-minute buckets. Zero means the source is idle.

targets.expr: ccloud_cdc:connector_records:rate10m{direction="out", connector_id=~"$source"} + on (connector_id) group_left (connector_name) (0 * max by (connector_id, connector_name) (confluent_kafka_connect_connector_status))

panels.title: Source batch size (avg / max records)
panels.description: Records per batch the source tasks hand to Kafka, worst task per connector. A max that sits flat at one value is pegged at the connector's max.batch.size, i.e. the ceiling is binding and batches are being cut by size rather than by time.

panels.title: Snapshot state
panels.description: Initial-snapshot state of each source connector that reports it: RUNNING while the snapshot is in progress, aborted if it was aborted, 'completed · streaming' once done. '—' means no snapshot metric is reporting a state. Not available for every connector type. These are the connector's own snapshot metrics: after a connector restart they can report aborted (and not completed) while streaming continues normally, so check source throughput and CDC lag before acting on it.

targets.expr: (3 * (max by (connector_id, connector_name) ({__name__=~"confluent_kafka_connect_(sql_server|postgres|mysql)_cdc_source_connector_snapshot_running", connector_id=~"$source"}) == 1)) or (2 * (max by (connector_id, connector_name) ({__name__=~"confluent_kafka_connect_(sql_server|postgres|mysql)_cdc_source_connector_snapshot_aborted", connector_id=~"$source"}) == 1)) or (1 * (max by (connector_id, connector_name) ({__name__=~"confluent_kafka_connect_(sql_server|postgres|mysql)_cdc_source_connector_snapshot_completed", connector_id=~"$source"}) == 1)) or (0 * max by (connector_id, connector_name) ({__name__=~"confluent_kafka_connect_(sql_server|postgres|mysql)_cdc_source_connector_snapshot_running", connector_id=~"$source"}))

panels.title: Sink put-batch time (avg / max, ms)
panels.description: Time the sink tasks spend writing one batch to the target system. 'avg' is the worst task average (the value used in the headline); 'max' is the worst single batch seen in the interval. Sustained growth points at the target system as the bottleneck.

panels.title: Sink throughput (records/s in)
panels.description: Records per second the sink connectors consume from Kafka, smoothed over 10 minutes from per-minute buckets. Compare with the source throughput: a sustained gap means a backlog is building.

targets.expr: ccloud_cdc:connector_records:rate10m{direction="in", connector_id=~"$sink"} + on (connector_id) group_left (connector_name) (0 * max by (connector_id, connector_name) (confluent_kafka_connect_connector_status))

panels.title: records_lag_max (fetch lag)
panels.description: Maximum number of records the sink's consumer is behind the end of the log. Near 0 means the sink reads Kafka immediately; if committed consumer lag is high anyway, it is likely offset-commit cadence rather than a real backlog.

panels.title: Sink batch size (avg / max records)
panels.description: Records per batch the sink tasks receive from Kafka, worst task per connector. This is the Kafka consume batch, capped by max.poll.records; it is not the connector's batch.size setting for writes to the target.

panels.title: Dead-letter-queue records per minute
panels.description: Records the sink connectors sent to the dead-letter queue in each 1-minute bucket. Any value above 0 is amber, above 100 is red. Records in the DLQ were not written to the target.

panels.title: Connector status
panels.description: Current status of each selected source and sink connector. RUNNING is green, PAUSED is blue, any other status (for example FAILED) is red. Only the most recently reported status is shown, so a status change is not hidden by the previous value.

targets.expr: confluent_kafka_connect_connector_status{connector_id=~"$source|$sink"} == 1 and on (connector_id, status) (timestamp(confluent_kafka_connect_connector_status{connector_id=~"$source|$sink"}) == on (connector_id) group_left () max by (connector_id) (timestamp(confluent_kafka_connect_connector_status{connector_id=~"$source|$sink"})))

panels.title: Task status
panels.description: Current status of each task of the selected source and sink connectors. RUNNING is green, PAUSED is blue, any other status (for example FAILED) is red. Only the most recently reported status is shown, so a status change is not hidden by the previous value.

targets.expr: confluent_kafka_connect_connector_task_status{connector_id=~"$source|$sink"} == 1 and on (connector_id, task, status) (timestamp(confluent_kafka_connect_connector_task_status{connector_id=~"$source|$sink"}) == on (connector_id, task) group_left () max by (connector_id, task) (timestamp(confluent_kafka_connect_connector_task_status{connector_id=~"$source|$sink"})))

title: Confluent Cloud CDC Pipeline Latency
